line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 d4 exd4 Nd5 h6
teaches: To win back a gambit pawn, attack the piece defending it rather than the pawn itself. Counting defenders first tells you which piece to harass, and a bishop that pins or hits the guard does more than a piece aimed at the pawn ever will.
explains: Black is a pawn up on d4 and the knight on c6 is what holds it. Two bishop developments come into consideration: one to d3, intending to swing round afterwards, and one straight to b5, which attacks the guard at once — once that knight is dealt with, both the knight and the queen are ready to collect on d4.
